details: The Federal Reserve has maintained its federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75%, signaling a continued "higher-for-longer" monetary policy outlook due to persistent inflation, despite some internal dissent. This environment has kept the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) and Treasury yields under scrutiny, contributing to a risk-off sentiment in the cryptocurrency market, with Bitcoin retreating towards the $63,000 mark. However, recent developments, including a significant drop in oil prices following reports of potential progress in a deal with Iran and an OPEC+ production increase, could offer some relief by easing inflation expectations. Cheaper oil may provide the Fed more flexibility for future rate adjustments.
title: Fed's "Higher-for-Longer" Stance Persists Amidst Fluctuating Inflation Signals

details: Hopes for the U.S. Senate to pass the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (CLARITY Act) in early August are reportedly diminishing. Analysts from Bernstein have indicated that the odds of the bill, which aims to clarify CFTC/SEC regulatory boundaries for digital assets, passing in 2026 are fading. This potential delay or dilution of the legislation could prolong regulatory uncertainty and trigger short-term profit-taking, particularly in altcoins that have been shadowed by "unregistered securities" concerns.
title: Optimism Fades for US CLARITY Act Passage in 2026

details: The U.S. dollar has continued its recent weakening trend against several major currencies. Historically, periods of dollar weakness have often coincided with increased investor interest in alternative assets such as equities, gold, and cryptocurrencies. This ongoing trend could create a more supportive environment for the cryptocurrency market by improving liquidity conditions and encouraging greater risk appetite among investors.
title: Weakening US Dollar Boosts Demand for Alternative Assets

details: Binance, a major cryptocurrency exchange, has announced it will delist six crypto tokens from its spot market on August 17, 2026. The tokens to be removed are Across Protocol (ACX), Hashflow (HFT), PIVX, Vulcan Forged PYR (PYR), Vanar (VANRY), and Viction (VIC). This decision follows Binance's periodic project review, which assesses factors such as liquidity, development team activity, network security, and regulatory considerations.
title: Binance to Delist Six Crypto Tokens in August
